group: PSI Score: Pneumonia Severity Index for CAP
question:
Patient note:
An 85-year-old woman who still maintains her own condominium and takes the city bus to her weekly bridge club was brought to the emergency department by her neighbor after two days of progressively louder cough, exertional breathlessness that began while climbing the single flight of stairs to her bedroom last night, and a measured oral fever of 39.7 °C that failed to abate with cool compresses; the neighbor purposely withheld acetaminophen, inhalers, or supplemental oxygen so that hospital staff could capture unaltered baseline readings. The patient relates that the illness started as a dry tickle but yesterday afternoon became productive of rust-colored sputum accompanied by shaking chills and a pleuritic ache just below the left scapula whenever she inhaled deeply. She denies headache, confusion, focal weakness, or visual changes and correctly states her birth date, location, and the current president during the interview. Her medical background includes a decade-long history of systolic heart dysfunction managed by a cardiologist with low-dose carvedilol and torsemide, and moderate chronic kidney impairment attributed to longstanding hypertension for which she follows a sodium-restricted diet; the most recent outpatient creatinine three months ago was 1.9 mg/dL with an estimated glomerular filtration rate in the mid-30s. She has never been told she had a stroke, transient ischemic attack, cirrhosis, or any form of malignancy, and she quit smoking cigarettes forty years ago after a 15-pack-year exposure. Medications taken the morning before symptom escalation include carvedilol 12.5 mg twice daily, torsemide 10 mg each morning, lisinopril 20 mg daily, calcium carbonate, and a daily vitamin; she does not use insulin, inhalers, anticoagulants, or narcotics. Vaccination records in the state registry show receipt of the seasonal influenza immunization last September and both pneumococcal series completed. Paramedics placed her on a monitor but administered no fluids, antipyretics, or oxygen during the twelve-minute transport. On arrival she sat upright on the gurney, speaking in full sentences between frequent paroxysms of cough, skin flushed and diaphoretic, but with brisk capillary refill and no peripheral edema. Untreated vital signs were: oral temperature 39.9 °C, regular radial pulse 129 beats per minute, non-invasive blood pressure 142/74 mm Hg confirmed manually, respiratory rate 49 breaths per minute with visible intercostal recruitment, and ambient-air fingertip oximetry fluctuating between 92 % and 93 % at this altitude of 150 m above sea level. Jugular venous pulsation was mildly elevated to the angle of the mandible when she lay supine at 30°, consistent with her cardiac baseline. Cardiac auscultation revealed a rapid but regular S1 and S2 with an audible third sound similar to prior clinic notes, no new murmurs or pericardial rub. Pulmonary examination demonstrated bronchial breath sounds and coarse crackles throughout the left lower posterior field with resonance to percussion, while the right lung was clear; no dullness or stony flatness suggesting free fluid was appreciated. The abdomen was soft and nontender, liver edge was not palpable, and bowel sounds were active. Neurologic screen showed equal reactive pupils, intact extra-ocular movements, 5/5 strength in all extremities, steady finger-nose testing, and a normal gait when she ambulated short distance to the scale. Capillary glucose measured immediately prior to vascular access was 95 mg/dL. Venous chemistries drawn within ten minutes of arrival (before any saline flushes or medications) returned sodium 114 mEq/L, potassium 3.8 mEq/L, chloride 88 mEq/L, bicarbonate 19 mEq/L, creatinine 2.0 mg/dL, and blood urea nitrogen 55 mg/dL. Complete blood count revealed leukocytes 14.7 × 10⁹/L with 90 % segmented neutrophils, hematocrit 61 %, hemoglobin 20.4 g/dL, and platelets 212 × 10⁹/L. A radial arterial sample while she remained on room air showed pH 7.63, PaCO₂ 28 mm Hg, PaO₂ 91 mm Hg, calculated bicarbonate 19 mEq/L, and base excess +4, reflecting a primary respiratory alkalosis with mild hypoxemia. Serum lactate was 1.4 mmol/L. High-sensitivity troponin was below the limit of detection. A portable postero-anterior chest radiograph obtained before any therapy demonstrated a dense consolidation occupying the lingula and lower lobe on the left with air bronchograms, sharp costophrenic angles, and a cardiac silhouette unchanged from an outpatient study six months prior; no layering opacity or meniscus was seen. Point-of-care ultrasound corroborated the absence of free pleural fluid and revealed hyperdynamic left ventricular function similar to her known compensated state. Electrocardiography displayed sinus tachycardia at 128 beats per minute with left ventricular hypertrophy voltage criteria but no acute ischemic changes. Two peripheral sets of blood cultures, an induced sputum sample for Gram stain and culture, urinary antigens for Streptococcus pneumoniae and Legionella, and a respiratory viral PCR panel were dispatched to the laboratory prior to the completion of this note. Up to this moment she has received no antipyretics, bronchodilators, supplemental oxygen, diuretics, intravenous crystalloids, vasopressors, or antimicrobial agents, ensuring that every physiological observation, vital sign, radiographic finding, and laboratory value documented above reflects her untreated state at the time of presentation.

Question: What is the patient's Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI)? You should use the patient's medical values and health status when they were first admitted to the hospital prior to any treatment.
solution:
The Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI) sums demographic, comorbidity, examination, laboratory, and radiographic points at presentation.
- Demographics: for a woman, use age minus 10: 85 − 10 = 75. She lives independently, so no nursing-home points.
- Comorbidities: systolic heart failure = 10; chronic renal disease = 10. No malignancy, liver disease, or cerebrovascular disease = 0 each.
- Examination: respiratory rate 49/min (≥30) = 20; pulse 129/min (≥125) = 10. She is oriented = 0; systolic BP 142 mm Hg (not <90) = 0; temperature 39.9 °C (neither <35 nor ≥40) = 0.
- Laboratory findings: BUN 55 mg/dL (≥30) = 20; sodium 114 mEq/L (<130) = 20. Arterial pH 7.63 (not <7.35), glucose 95 mg/dL (not ≥250), hematocrit 61% (not <30%), and PaO₂ 91 mm Hg (not <60) = 0 each.
- Imaging: no pleural effusion = 0.
Total = 75 + 10 + 10 + 20 + 10 + 20 + 20 = 165.
Final answer: 165
